questions.correct: Three numbers: x, y, and heading
wrong: A single number: the robot's speed
Two numbers: motor power and time
A list of every button ever pressed
questions.explain: A pose is (x, y, heading) — where the robot is on the field and which way it faces. It's the robot's full "where am I" in three numbers.

questions.correct: Figuring out distance by counting wheel turns
wrong: Measuring the battery's charge over time
Reading the heading from a compass app
Counting how many pieces are stored inside
questions.explain: Odometry works out how far you've traveled by counting wheel turns — just like a car's odometer. Pinpoint uses it to track the robot's pose.

questions.correct: An unpowered wheel that rolls freely to measure
wrong: A drive wheel that has completely burned out
A wheel that has no rubber tread left on it
A spare wheel kept in the pit for repairs
questions.explain: A dead wheel has no motor, so it coasts and rolls cleanly without slipping. That makes its turn count an accurate measure of distance.

questions.q: How are the two tracking pods mounted?
questions.correct: 90 degrees apart, one for X and one for Y
wrong: Right next to each other, both tracking X
On the same axle, sharing one encoder
On top of the two front drive motors
questions.explain: Two pods sit 90° apart: one tracks forward/back (X) and one tracks sideways (Y). Together they catch motion in any direction.

wrong: Backward
To the right
Straight down
questions.explain: The field frame is +X forward, +Y left, +heading counter-clockwise. Drive forward and x goes up.

wrong: To the right
Forward
Backward
questions.explain: +Y points left. Strafe left and y grows; strafe right and it shrinks. Forward is +X and turning left grows the heading.

questions.q: Which I2C port must you NOT use for Pinpoint?
questions.correct: Port 0, because the built-in IMU lives there
wrong: Port 3, because it is far too slow
Port 1, because it is always reserved
Any port at all; they all conflict badly
questions.explain: The hub's built-in IMU already uses I2C Port 0, so plugging Pinpoint there causes conflicts. Use Port 1, 2, or 3 instead.

questions.correct: The straight-line distance from the start
wrong: The robot's current heading in radians
The battery's remaining charge percent
The number of loops run so far
questions.explain: Math.hypot(x, y) is the Pythagorean distance — how far the robot is from where it started, straight-line, using √(x² + y²).

questions.q: What must you call each loop to keep the pose fresh?
questions.correct: The Pinpoint's update, to pull the latest pose
wrong: The telemetry update, to redraw the screen
The battery check, to read the voltage
The intake command, to keep it spinning
questions.explain: You have to refresh Pinpoint every loop (its update) or the pose freezes at its last reading. Localization is only useful when it's current.

questions.q: If a pod is mounted crooked, then...
questions.correct: Forward and sideways readings get mixed up
wrong: The battery drains about twice as fast
The flywheel spins at the wrong RPM
The telemetry stops printing its lines
questions.explain: A crooked pod blends the X and Y motion together, so the tracked position drifts off. Pods must be square to the frame for clean readings.

questions.q: Turning the robot left (counter-clockwise) makes heading...
wrong: Go down
Stay the same
Reset to zero
questions.explain: +heading is counter-clockwise, so turning left grows the heading and turning right shrinks it. Zero is the starting direction.

questions.correct: A computer that reads dead wheels and a gyro for pose
wrong: A camera that films the entire match
A motor that drives the tracking wheels
A battery that powers the odometry pods
questions.explain: The goBILDA Pinpoint is a small computer that reads two dead wheels plus a gyro and continuously reports the robot's pose over I2C.

questions.q: Why do dead wheels roll without slipping?
questions.correct: They have no motor, so they just coast
wrong: They are much heavier than drive wheels
They spin twice as fast as drive wheels
They are made of a special grippy metal
questions.explain: A powered wheel can slip when it spins; a dead wheel has no motor, so it simply follows the floor. That clean rolling makes its count accurate.

questions.q: The config name the code looks up must...
questions.correct: Match the name in the configuration exactly
wrong: Always be spelled in all capital letters
Be different from the code's device name
Include the robot battery's voltage
questions.explain: hardwareMap looks up the device by name, so "pinpoint" in the config must match "pinpoint" in the code exactly — spelling and case included.

questions.q: Why does field-centric driving depend on good localization?
questions.correct: A wrong +Y direction would steer paths sideways
wrong: The flywheel needs the pose to spin up
The intake can't run without a valid pose
The battery charges from the odometry pods
questions.explain: If the frame is wrong (say +Y points the wrong way), every heading-based move steers off. Correct pod directions keep field-centric and autonomous on target.
